thread:
sanjay: Heads-up: I'm scheduling the 2.1.0-quant-kernel push to staging at 09:30 PT. It's the new matmul change + updated fp16 path. Will run the usual smoke + long-seq perf sweep.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: target=staging, build=engine-2.1.0-quant1, id=stg-20260310-01 :rocket:

amanda: thanks. can we run the thermal/longseq test with 32k tokens and kv-cache stress? last time we saw cold-start spike.

sanjay: yes. plan: smoke (1k seq), longseq (32k, 4x concurrency), kv-evict probe. I'll post the commands.

lucy: tagging @maya-oncall for oncall oversight during the window. also adding the release notes blurb draft below.

lucy: Release notes (draft): "Engine 2.1.0-quant1: performance improvements for matmul kernels, improved fp16 stability, and reduced memory for KV-cache. Recommend for staging verification before stable rollout."

rafael: Important: this build changes kernel ABI for cuBLAS wrapper. Compatibility matrix updated: some old pinned images will fail. Need to confirm dedicated pools won't accidentally pick this build.

amanda: can we add an automatic pin TTL on dedicated pools during rollout? i.e., prevent universal swap until we manually unpin?

sanjay: yes — plan is to push to staging, then push to canary routing only for hosted tier, not dedicated. We'll set a sticky pin on dedicated with TTL=24h. deploy-bot supports pin via: 

```
# pin dedicated pools during rollout
deploy-bot pin --target=dedicated --build=engine-2.1.0-quant1 --ttl=24h
```

maya-oncall: I'll be watching telemetry. What are concrete rollback triggers? please enumerate so oncall can act without pinging you.

lucy: proposed rollback criteria (staging -> canary):
- 5xx rate increase > 0.5% absolute and sustained for 5m
- tail latency P99 increase > 200ms for 10m
- token error rate (invalid outputs / hallucinations) increase > 1.0% on eval prompts
- memory OOMs observed on >=2 nodes in same AZ

rafael: add: mismatch between kernel checksum reported by runtime and expected image checksum (indicates packaging bug) -> immediate rollback.

amanda: also add degradation in generation quality on canary eval set: BLEU/ROUGE drop >3 points or embedding cosine drop >0.05 vs baseline. We have the eval job configured at: https://internal.rw/evals/job/engine-quant-canary

sanjay: good. will bake those as alerts in the release runbook. Also adding a soft hold: if any customer-facing SLA for dedicated is impacted, we automatically stop routing to canary.

deploy-bot: canary route update: canary=10% hosted, dedicated=no, region=us-west-2. Starting canary now.

amanda: starting smoke commands locally: 
```
# smoke
python tools/smoke.py --host stg.rw --build engine-2.1.0-quant1 --seq 1000 --concurrency 2
# longseq perf
python tools/longseq.py --host stg.rw --build engine-2.1.0-quant1 --seq 32000 --concurrency 4 --kv-stress
```

lucy: smoke passed on 3/3 matmul tests. longseq warmup looks okay but one node had elevated transient mem on first run. tagged logs: https://internal.rw/logs/edge/abc123

maya-oncall: seeing P99 bump in one AZ from 180ms -> 420ms starting 09:48. it's on two canary instances. Investigating whether it's warm-start related.

rafael: can we repro in staging with a single-node pinned job? run warm-restart sequence and watch kernel loader logs.

sanjay: running repro with pinned instance now. command: 
```
ssh runtime@stg-node-17
sudo journalctl -u runtime -f | grep -i kernel
# then kick longseq client
```

amanda: note from logs: `kernel_loader: warning: quant_kernel_v2 checksum mismatch fallback applied` — that's the checksum mismatch case.

rafael: that's the packaging bug scenario. rollback criterion met. we should roll back canary and unpin dedicated.

sanjay: agreed. rolling back canary and unpin TTL. deploy-bot, please execute rollback to engine-2.0.9 and clear pins.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated: target=canary(hosted), from=engine-2.1.0-quant1 -> to=engine-2.0.9. Actions queued: route-swap, health-check, clear-pin(dedicated). id=rb-20260310-01 :white_check_mark:

lucy: filing release note note: "Rollback: engine-2.1.0-quant1 due to packaging checksum mismatch leading to fallback kernel and transient P99 increases on canary." I'll append remediation steps.

amanda: remediation TODOs: - fix packaging to preserve kernel checksums in manifest - add preflight checksum verify in image build step - expand longseq smoke in CI - add automated TTL pin when packaging ABI changes

maya-oncall: after rollback, keep watch for residual OOMs. I'll monitor but unpin dedicated so customers unaffected.

rafael: creating follow-up PRs and issue for packaging fix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5234

sanjay: thanks everyone. lessons learned: pin dedicated early, run checksum preflight in CI, ensure canary eval set includes kernel checksum monitor. We'll reschedule a new candidate once packaging fix merges and CI passes. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Rollback complete: status=success, time=09:57 PT, id=rb-20260310-01

lucy: closing the thread for now. I'll open a post-mortem doc with notes and release timeline.

sanjay: +1. thanks all for quick action.
